title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime is zero fibre dimension at that point
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset T$ be prime and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Put $F=T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\overline{\mathfrak q}\in\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be the unique prime contracting to $\mathfrak q$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Then $\varphi$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] if and only if $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}\operatorname{Spec}F=0$, where dimension at a point is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].
